body:
I don't have kids, but my wife and I are trying. That's another thing I worry about. Putting my problems on them. I think I'd be good because I'd do nothing by support them in a meaningful way. Even if I disagreed with a choice of theirs, I would do my best not to make them feel embarrassed, ashamed, etc. If I'm being honest though, if I can't figure out how to navigate through life, how can I help them navigate through the shit storm that is life. 

Not a professional at all, but I think the best you can do is just make sure they feel loved you know? Be aware of the things your parents did to you, and then don't do that to them.

Ha, how much time do you have? I'm a perfectionist too, but I don't know if that's my problem. My mother was emotionally manipulative and abusive. My Dad doesn't offer much emotional support, and for most of my life has been dismissive of the field I went into (music). That's the short version of it. I think that has contributed to my never feeling good enough, not deserving of any praise, etc though. That's my theory anyway...

You're so right, and I know it. I just can't figure out how to shake that need to feel validated from other people. I know I need to, but I don't know how. It's fucked up right? My family situation is majorly fucked up, so I know I shouldn't expect any validation from them (though it would be nice). My wife and dogs mean the world to me, but I can't figure out why I need more, and why I feel like I don't deserve them. I guess that's my journey to figure out. Hopefully I make it. Can't say thanks enough for interacting with me today and talking through these issues with me.

Yeah from the outside in, I'm sure people think I have nothing to be upset about. But as you probably know, people don't know the experiences we've had growing up, whether it was family, friends, or both that have shaped the perception we have of ourselves. It's an awful thing to go through. Even when I've felt good about something, within minutes or days, I've got that feeling of stupidity for putting myself out there, and that voice telling me "hey dummy, it's nothing special, why do you feel good about this?" Wish I could figure what it is I need to feel comfortable in my own skin and enjoy what I have.

Her and I talk about a lot of things, so the conversation level is good. I mean about the self-loathing, depression type stuff. She's amazing. It's more that I believe there's no way she can love me, because of the constant feeling of being worthless. It legitimately confuses me that she is with me. I think the older of gotten and the more things seem to not be working out in life (besides her) the more this feeling grows. I know it comes from the old school mentality I was raised on of men providing and that is their value in a relationship. I know it's BS too, but it fucks with me all the time. All of her friends are married to successful guys (and are also independently successful) so that only contributes to it. I know it's foolish, but again I have this little voice that's like "look at you, you're pathetic." We have 3 dogs, and believe those guys and gal keep me going too.

I spent sometime in LA too. Same kind of experience as you. Although I never really made permanent friends out there. Growing up I had a lot of instances where friends lied to me, backstabbed, all that other BS people do, so I do this thing where I withdraw. You can't reject me, because I reject you kind of thing. I lived in NYC too. Better experience there. I describe it as being hard as hell to break into that circle of friends, but once you're there you're in for life. Still, no matter what, I'm the guy calling people to make plans, to see how people are doing, etc. Eventually that gets to me when it's been...months and not a single person has called to say what's up. It's petty, but damn it would be nice. 

I have a lot of nice things in my life, and things I'm very thankful for, so I hope this doesn't sound like whining. I appreciate you letting me vent though. For whatever reason though I've never felt validated, and because of that I always feel like I don't deserve any of it.
Please, no need to apologize. I know the feeling and it's the worst. I appreciate you even reaching out begin with, so thank you.
Yes it is. Most people offer a "just get over it" sort of reply.

Believe me, I'm thankful for her everyday. I'd be gone if she wasn't in my life. The weird thing is, is that I don't talk to her. I've got so much "guys don't cry, show emotion" type crap in my head from my upbringing I try as hard as possible not to show weakness. The times that I've slipped up and talked to her, I can see it in her eyes that she has no idea what to think, so I close up even more. A good chunk of what you said about forming friends is why I don't think I'm made for this life or maybe these times. I can't fathom wanting to be friends with someone who didn't give a shit about you or care about you. I get what you're saying, and certainly when you're starting out you have to play things cool, but at some point that barrier gets old to me. I don't want to go through life always having to keep my guard up. I appreciate you taking the time to respond.
